transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (CTO, Oasis), Liam Chen (ML Eng), Sophie Alvarez (PM)
---
[00:00:05] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the account executive working with you. Uh, quick round robin?
[00:00:13] Priya: Priya here, CTO at Oasis Health. We've got Liam and Sophie on as well.
[00:00:18] Liam: Hey. Liam, ML eng.
[00:00:20] Sophie: Sophie, product. Thanks for running this.
[00:00:24] Ethan: Hi, Ethan Ross, solutions engineer. I'll talk technical stuff, benchmarks, that kind of thing.
[00:00:30] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to understand your retrieval/rerank workflow, current infra, pain points around latency/cost, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private deployment makes sense — and outline next steps.
[00:00:45] Sophie: Yeah, perfect. I'll give a quick overview of what we're trying to solve.
[00:00:50] Sophie: So Oasis is building a clinician search product, internal and external search across patient education, knowledge base, triage notes. Right now we use Elastic for full-text and some boolean queries, but relevance drops for semantic queries, so we're looking at embeddings + rerank to improve top-k.
[00:01:10] Priya: High level constraints: must keep PHI off third-party systems unless we have BAAs and encryption at rest; latency target for patient-facing features is <= 300ms median end-to-end; throughput during peak is roughly 120 qps for search API, but many are small payloads. Cost is also a major constraint — we can't multiply cost per query by 5x.
[00:01:36] Ethan: Got it. When you say PHI off third-party systems, do you already have a VPC or private cloud setup that you'd want Redwood Private to hook into?
[00:01:42] Priya: We have an AWS VPC and an internal KMS. Ideally we'd like control over keys and logs. We're open to Hosted if you offer Customer‑managed keys and a BAA, otherwise Dedicated or Private looks likely.
[00:01:55] Maya: Redwood does SOC 2 and we support KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have an enterprise package with a BAA and bring-your-own-key via our KMS integrations — we can share the security pack.
[00:02:06] Sophie: Nice. On the embeddings side — Liam, can you share current setup?
[00:02:10] Liam: Sure. We're experimenting with 1536-d embeddings using an off-the-shelf instruction-tuned model. Right now we host vectors in Milvus for internal proofs. Retrieval is ANN via HNSW, then we do a transformer-based cross-encoder for rerank which is heavy. We're curious about two things: 1) whether Redwood can host embeddings and rerank in a single pipeline, and 2) how you'd integrate with our vector DB — do we keep Milvus or move to Pinecone?
[00:02:38] Ethan: Good questions. Short answers: Redwood's Hosted API can return embeddings and also do generation/reranking calls; for high-throughput rerank we typically recommend an architecture where embeddings are stored in your vector DB and Redwood performs lightweight candidate scoring and optionally sends candidates to a reranker hosted in Dedicated/Private or in your infra depending on latency needs. We integrate with vector DBs via a simple retrieval step — we don't replace your DB unless you want us to.
[00:02:58] Maya: To add, some customers use a hybrid approach: Elastic/BM25 for recall + embeddings for semantic top-k, then Redwood for rerank or for the final cross-encoder. That helps reduce cost because you only rerank a small candidate set.
[00:03:13] Sophie: That hybrid approach sounds like what we want. Our product team wants the best relevance but also consistent latency.
[00:03:20] Liam: Regarding dimensionality — 1536 is what we're testing but we've also seen 768 embeddings from some models perform well with reduced cost. How sensitive is Redwood to embedding size in terms of throughput?
[00:03:31] Ethan: Embedding dimensionality mainly affects storage and vector DB indexing/ANN performance. On the Redwood side, larger embeddings increase network payload and slightly increase compute for batched similarity ops. For Hosted small-batch inference, it's negligible; for high QPS (100s qps), it matters. We also recommend quantized vectors in DB where possible.
[00:03:48] Priya: For our peak 120 qps — if we do a BM25 prefilter to 50 candidates and then embed and rerank, what kind of latency might we expect for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:03:58] Ethan: If your reranker is a cross-encoder that runs on a GPU, Dedicated gives predictable latency — you can tune batch size to keep median under 200ms for a 50-candidate rerank with optimized kernels. Hosted can hit that too but at higher per-query cost and occasional variance as multi-tenant capacity fluctuates. Private gives you lowest variance but requires you to manage infra.
[00:04:16] Maya: Also worth calling out our automatic prefix/KV caching — for conversational flows, but for static rerank caches across common queries can cut tokens. For rerank specifically, caching candidate embeddings or reranker outputs can help if there's query repetition.
[00:04:29] Liam: Do you have native connectors for Milvus? We currently index in Milvus and it's been fine for scale but we'd evaluate switching if there's a big operational upside.
[00:04:36] Ethan: We have customers using Milvus and Pinecone; integration is straightforward. For Milvus we typically recommend configuring HNSW parameters for recall/latency tradeoffs. If you want managed vector DB we can recommend partners, but we don't force a switch.
[00:04:48] Sophie: On data residency/compliance — can Hosted provision in a specific region and maintain audit logs tied to our account?
[00:04:55] Maya: Yes, Hosted supports region scoping and we can provide per-customer audit logs. For enterprise packages we can add longer retention in the Console. Dedicated and Private naturally give more control.
[00:05:04] Priya: Could you share any real-world perf numbers for similar deployments?
[00:05:08] Ethan: Yeah, e.g., a health search customer did BM25 -> 40 candidates -> cross-encoder rerank on Dedicated GPUs and saw median latency ~180ms and 95th around 320ms at 80 qps sustained. Hosted was similar median but 95th had more variance. We can share a benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:05:24] Liam: Great. About reranker model size — we're currently using a small T5 cross-encoder. Could Redwood host custom rerank models or do we bring our own?
[00:05:33] Ethan: Both. For Hosted we can host common open models; for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own container and model artifacts. We support quantized weights and optimized kernels, and we can help with compilation/kernels to speed up inference.
[00:05:46] Sophie: How does billing work if we do embeddings retrieval from our DB and then call Redwood for rerank only? Is it tokens-based or per-call?
[00:05:54] Maya: Rerank/generation calls are billed per-token for Hosted API for models that use generation, but for dedicated capacity you sign reserved capacity and pay for committed GPUs plus a per-request unit for usage outside the commit. We can run a TCO example for your query volume.
[00:06:07] Priya: For PHI concerns — BAA required, logs must be exportable to our SIEM, and KMS is required. Does Redwood's Hosted option support bring-your-own-key?
[00:06:16] Maya: Yes, BYOK for enterprise Hosted, and Dedicated/Private integrate with your KMS. We'll include SOC 2 report + security docs.
[00:06:24] Ethan: For benchmarks — if you can provide a sample of 10k anonymized docs and a representative query set, we can run retrieval + rerank tests against both Hosted and Dedicated configs and show latency/cost comparisons.
[00:06:36] Liam: We can do that. We'll have to scrub PHI.
[00:06:39] Sophie: Is there an easy way to do hybrid BM25 + embeddings in Redwood or is that on our side?
[00:06:44] Ethan: We provide SDKs and reference architectures that show how to do hybrid search — Elastic/Milvus + Redwood rerank. In some cases customers use our edge workers to run BM25 locally and then call Redwood for embeddings/rerank.
[00:06:56] Priya: Any gotchas for autoscaling during peak traffic? We need to make sure the reranker keeps up without huge cold-starts.
[00:07:03] Ethan: With Dedicated you configure GPU pools and autoscaling policies with warm pools for quick spin-up. For Hosted we have burst capacity but you might see slight cold-start tail latency during sudden spikes. Private is fully under your control.
[00:07:13] Maya: We'll include recommended autoscale policies and how to set warm pools.
[00:07:17] Sophie: On instrumentation — can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency in the console?
[00:07:22] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token cost breakdowns, and traces to map requests end-to-end.
[00:07:29] Liam: For rerank throughput, if we batch 8 queries together to the GPU reranker what's the expected improvement?
[00:07:35] Ethan: Throughput improves sub-linearly with batch size, and latency per query improves up to a point — but for small tail-latency sensitive features you tune batch size carefully. We can show profiling from similar workloads.
[00:07:47] Priya: This is helpful — looks like we should run a pilot comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for our 120 qps peak with BM25 prefilter to 50.
[00:07:56] Maya: Agreed. Proposed next steps: I'll send pricing/TCO, security pack, and a pilot proposal. Ethan will schedule a technical deep dive and ask for sample dataset. Liam will send dataset.
[00:08:08] Sophie: Sounds good.
[00:08:10] Priya: Quick question — any known limits on embedding dimensionality for your endpoints? We have a model doing 3072 dims in research, just curious.
[00:08:18] Ethan: No hard limits, but large embedding sizes increase payloads and memory footprint. For 3072 you'd want to test memory and ANN index performance; we can support it but may recommend reducing dimension or using PCA/quantization pre-indexing.
[00:08:30] Maya: Okay I'll follow up with a checklist for the pilot and the security docs.
[00:08:36] Liam: Thanks.
[00:08:38] Ethan: Thanks all.
[00:08:40] Maya: Recap of action items and I'll drop the links in CRM and send calendar invites for the deep-dive.
[00:08:47] Priya: Thanks, bye.
